'''''Nuphar pumila''''', the '''least water-lily''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> is a perennial,<ref name = "PFAF" /> rhizomatous, aquatic<ref name = "POWO a" /> herb<ref name = "NatureGate">Least Water-lily Nuphar pumila. (n.d.). LuontoPortti – NatureGate. Retrieved January 31, 2025, from https://luontoportti.com/en/t/2314/least-water-lily</ref> in the family [[Nymphaeaceae]] native to subarctic and temperate Eurasia.<ref name = "POWO a" />

== Description ==
[[File:Nuphar pumila (Timm) DC. rhizome.jpg|thumb|right|Rhizome of ''Nuphar pumila'' with scale bar (10 cm)]]
===Vegetative characteristics===
''Nuphar pumila'' is a perennial,<ref name = "Dynowski et al., 2016" /><ref name = "PFAF">''Nuphar pumila'' - (Timm.)DC. (n.d.). Plants for a Future (PFAF). Retrieved January 31, 2025, from https://pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Nuphar+pumila</ref> rhizomatous, aquatic<ref name = "POWO a" /> herb<ref name = "NatureGate" /> with 20–70 cm long,<ref name = "Dynowski et al., 2016" /> and 1–3 cm wide rhizomes.<ref name = "Flora of China" /> The ovate<ref name = "Dynowski et al., 2016" /> leaves are 5–10(–13) cm long,<ref name = "InfoFlora">''Nuphar pumila'' (Timm) DC. (n.d.). InfoFlora. Retrieved January 31, 2025, from https://www.infoflora.ch/de/flora/nuphar-pumila.html</ref> and 6–12 cm wide. The pubescent petiole is 20–50 cm long.<ref name = "Flora of China" /> The submerged leaves are round and wrinkled.<ref name = "NatureGate" />
===Generative characteristics===
The yellow,<ref name = "Flora of China" /> actinomorphic,<ref name = "NatureGate" /> faintly fragrant,<ref name = "FloraWeb">Bundesamt für Naturschutz. (n.d.). ''Nuphar pumila'' (Timm) DC. (Zwerg-Teichrose). FloraWeb. Retrieved January 31, 2025, from https://www.floraweb.de/php/artenhome.php?name-use-id=3858</ref> 1–4.5(–6) cm wide flowers have pubescent, 40–50 cm long peduncles<ref name = "Flora of China" /> The five<ref name = "Candolle, 1821" /> ovate to spathulate  sepals are 16–29 mm long, and 9–16 mm wide.<ref name = "Padgett, 1998">Padgett, D. J. (1998). [https://scholar.archive.org/work/6jz3swupubgcposlwi2kaltlnu/access/wayback/http://webhost.bridgew.edu/dpadgett/microphylla%20reprint.pdf Phenetic distinction between the dwarf yellow water-lilies: ''Nuphar microphylla'' and ''N. pumila'' (Nymphaeaceae).] Canadian journal of botany, 76(10), 1755-1762.</ref> The abaxial surface of the sepals is often green.<ref name = "InfoFlora" /> The flower has 9–13 petals.<ref name = "Padgett, 1998" /> The androecium consists of 35–65 stamens. The gynoecium consists of 7–12 carpels.<ref name = "Rothmaler">Müller, F., Ritz, C. M., Wesche, K., & Welk, E. (2021). [https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-662-61011-4 Rothmaler - Exkursionsflora von Deutschland. Gefäßpflanzen: Grundband.] p. 131. Springer Spektrum.</ref> The star-shaped stigmatic disk with 7–12 stigmatic rays is 6–8.5 mm wide.<ref name = "FloraWeb" /> The green,<ref name = "Padgett, 1998" /> 1–2 cm wide fruit<ref name = "Flora of China" /> bears greenish brown,<ref name = "Padgett, 1998" /> ovoid to oblong, 3–5 mm long seeds.<ref name = "Flora of China" />

==Cytology==
The chromosome count is 2n = 34.<ref name = "Flora of China" /> The chloroplast genome is 160737 bp long.<ref name = "He et al., 2018">He, D., Gichira, A. W., Li, Z., Nzei, J. M., Guo, Y., Wang, Q., & Chen, J. (2018). [https://www.preprints.org/manuscript/201811.0071/download/final_file Resolution of Intergeneric Relationships within the Early-Diverging Angiosperm Family Nymphaeaceae Based on Chloroplast Phylogenomics.]</ref>

==Taxonomy==
It was first published as the variety ''Nymphaea lutea'' var. ''pumila'' {{au|Timm}} by [[Joachim Christian Timm]] in 1795.<ref name = "POWO a" /> Later, it was elevated to the status of the separate species ''Nuphar pumila'' {{au|(Timm) DC.}} published by [[Augustin Pyramus de Candolle]] in 1821.<ref name = "Candolle, 1821">Candolle,  Augustin Pyramus de. (1818). Regni vegetabilis systema naturale, sive Ordines, genera et species plantarum secundum methodi naturalis normas digestarum et descriptarum (Vol. 2, p. 61). sumptibus sociorum Treuttel et Würtz. https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/39511861</ref><ref name = "POWO a" /> It is placed in the section [[Nuphar sect. Nuphar|''Nuphar'' sect. ''Nuphar'']].<ref name = "GRIN">USDA, Agricultural Research Service, National Plant Germplasm System. 2025. Germplasm Resources Information Network (GRIN Taxonomy). National Germplasm Resources Laboratory, Beltsville, Maryland.
URL: https://npgsweb.ars-grin.gov/gringlobal/taxon/taxonomydetail?id=416169. Accessed 19 February 2025.
</ref>
===Etymology===
The specific epithet ''pumila'' means small.<ref>A Grammatical Dictionary of Botanical Latin. (n.d.). Missouri Botanical Garden. Retrieved February 1, 2025, from https://www.mobot.org/mobot/latindict/keyDetail.aspx?keyWord=pumilus</ref><ref>Lagenophora pumila. (n.d.). New Zealand Plant Conservation Network. Retrieved February 1, 2025, from https://www.nzpcn.org.nz/flora/species/lagenophora-pumila/</ref>

== Distribution ==
''Nuphar pumila'' is native to China, Japan, Korea, Mongolia, Russia,<ref name = "Flora of China">''Nuphar pumila'' in Flora of China @ efloras.org. (n.d.). Retrieved January 31, 2025, from http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=242000581</ref> Switzerland,<ref name = "InfoFlora" /> the United Kingdom,<ref name = "PFAF" /> Austria, Germany, France, Spain,<ref name = "Arrigo et al., 2016" /> Finland, Sweden, Denmark, and Poland.<ref name = "POWO a" />

In Europe, the typical subspecies ''Nuphar pumila'' subsp. ''pumila'' is present.<ref name = "Arrigo et al., 2016" />

==Conservation==
The [[IUCN]] conservation status is least concern (LC).<ref name = "IUCN" /> However, it is threatened by [[Nuphar × spenneriana|hybridisation with ''Nuphar lutea'']],<ref name = "Arrigo et al., 2016">Arrigo, N., Bétrisey, S., Graf, L., Bilat, J., Gerber, E., & Kozlowski, G. (2016). [https://folia.unifr.ch/documents/305241/files/koz_htc.pdf Hybridization as a threat in climate relict ''Nuphar pumila'' (Nymphaeaceae).] Biodiversity and Conservation, 25, 1863-1877.</ref><ref name = "Keller, 2018" /><ref name = "Buchholz, 2023" /><ref name = "InfoFlora" /> climate change,<ref name = "Buchholz, 2023">Alfred Buchholz (2023): [https://www.lfu.bayern.de/natur/gutachten/detail.htm?id=9a0bsa2 Artenhilfsprogramm Kleine Teichrose ''Nuphar pumila'' in Bayern.] - Unveröffentlichtes Gutachten im Auftrag von: Bayerisches Landesamt für Umwelt, 25 Seiten, Augsburg.</ref> pollution, and habitat destruction.<ref name = "InfoFlora" /> It is classified as endangered in Switzerland,<ref name = "Keller, 2018">Keller, S. (2018). [https://digitalcollection.zhaw.ch/bitstreams/4fb9896e-e48e-4643-8ec7-3f1fb2ebe056/download Ansiedlung der Kleinen Teichrose ''Nuphar pumila'': Vergleich der Standortbedingungen in erfolgreichen und erfolglosen Ansiedlungsgewässern.] In Bachelorarbeit Umweltingenieurwesen ZHAW Wädenswil IUNR, unveröffentlicht.</ref> vulnerable in France,<ref name = "INPN">MNHN & OFB [Ed]. 2003-2025. Sheet of ''Nuphar pumila'' (Timm) DC., 1821. Inventaire national du patrimoine naturel (INPN). Website: https://inpn.mnhn.fr/espece/cd_nom/109735 - January 31, 2025</ref> and endangered in Poland.<ref name = "Dynowski et al., 2016">Dynowski, P., Herbich, J., Źróbek-Sokolnik, A., Dziedzic, J., & Kozłowski, J. (2016). [http://www.uwm.edu.pl/polish-journal/sites/default/files/issues/articles/dynowski_et_al._2016.pdf A new stand and the current status of the ''Nuphar pumila'' population in Warminsko-Mazurskie province.] Pol. J. Nat. Sci, 31, 587-598.</ref>

==Ecology==
===Habitat===
It occurs in lakes, ponds<ref name = "Flora of China" /> and slowly flowing rivers<ref name = "NatureGate" /> in nutrient-poor waters at depths of 0.5–3 m.<ref name = "InfoFlora" />
===Herbivory===
The leaf mine species ''[[Hydromyza livens]]'' feeds on ''Nuphar pumila'' leaves.<ref name = "Bladmineerders">''Nuphar pumila'' – Plant Parasites of Europe. (n.d.). Retrieved January 31, 2025, from https://bladmineerders.nl/host-plants/plantae/spermatopsida/angiosperma/nymphaeales/nymphaeaceae/nuphar/nuphar-pumila/</ref>

==Common names==
''Nuphar pumila'' is also known as least water lily<ref name = "EPPO" /> or least yellow water-lily.<ref name = "NatureGate" />

== Uses ==
It is cultivated as an ornamental plant.<ref name = "EPPO">''Nuphar pumila'' (NUPPU). (n.d.). EPPO Global Database. Retrieved January 31, 2025, from https://gd.eppo.int/taxon/NUPPU</ref>
